newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see flood of dollar deals in busy sessioN.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see flood of dollar deals in busy sessioN.

text.p: Volumes surged in the primary market on Wednesday following a quiet start to the week.
The dollar sector in particular was busy, but deals surfaced in marks, French francs, guilders and New Zealand dollar too.
"Issuance in dollars is supported by the stong flows we are still seeing in that currency," a syndicate manager at a European bank said.
"Demand in Europe is mainly focused on the shorter end of the curve, but Japanese investors are buying 10-year paper."
Reflecting this, Kyushu Electric Power issued a $300 million 10-year bond, priced to yield 37 basis points over Treasuries.
Bankers said the issue was doing well, with the pricing comparing favourably to outstanding issues.

An Osaka Gas Co bond maturing in February 2007 was trading at 40 b.p. over, and is rated AA2/AA- compared with Kyushu's AA1 rating. A triple-A rated Tokyo Electric Power 10-year bond is trading in the high-20s b.p. over, traders said.
On the corporate side, Carrefour Supermarche launched a debut international bond, a $250 million three-year deal priced to yield 20 b.p. over Treasuries.
An official at lead manager BZW said this was Carrefour's, France's largest retailer, first international bond issue and was launched after extensive meetings with European investors.

Carrefour is unrated, and this meant some investors were unable to buy the paper, the official said. Demand for the deal was strong out of Benelux and Switzerland in particular, because the issue provided a yield pick-up over other paper.
Bayerische Vereinsbank, rated AA1, on Tuesday launched a $200 million three-year bond at 10 b.p. over. Last week IBM, rated A1/A, issued a similar deal at 15 b.p. over Treasuries.
Another debut bond was launched by German sports car maker Porsche. Bankers said the 200 million mark five-year bond was snapped up due to its strong name recognition.

In French francs, Ford Motor Credit launch two 1.5 billion franc bonds, one with a six-year maturity and another for 12 years. Dealers said the issues were well-received, yielding around three b.p. below where outstanding Ford paper is trading.
Banque Nationale de Paris launched a 1.25 billion franc step-up perpetual bond, an unusual structure for the sector.
"It is good to see this development in the French market, where there have been few such deals," a syndicate manager involved in the transaction said.
"French banks have traditionally had to go to the dollar and sterling markets for upper tier two capital," he said.
